page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-288 is a compute-optimized instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 288 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 144 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor running at 2.3 GHz. The system is equipped with 576 GB of RAM, providing a 2.0 GB per core memory-to-vCPU ratio. The processor includes a 504 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1D cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU scores and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 1088.77 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 448.45 GB/sec for writes. The instance excels in parallelized tasks, as shown by top-tier results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, software compilation with Clang, and ray tracing. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench text processing scoring in the middle 50%. While LLM prompt processing and medium-to-large model text generation perform strongly, text generation for small 135M models is relatively weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highcpu-288 offers high compute density and massive parallel processing capabilities without the added expense of GPU hardware or local storage. This makes it highly suitable for CPU-bound, highly parallelized workloads. Recommended use cases include large-scale software compilation, high-throughput database operations, static web serving, multi-threaded data compression, and CPU-based LLM inference.
